issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement and UML require the Farm to aggregate animals using a List and explicitly instruct to initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. The solution implementation instead declares animals as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with new LinkedList<>(), causing a type mismatch between the specified attribute type (List/ArrayList) and the solution's attribute type (Queue/LinkedList). This inconsistency can confuse students about which collection type and getter/setter signatures they must implement and which concrete collection to instantiate.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution's Farm to declare private List<Animal> animals; initialize it in the no-arg constructor with new ArrayList<>(); and update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. For example: private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } public List<Animal> getAnimals() { return animals; } public void setAnimals(List<Animal> animals) { this.animals = animals; } and ensure addAnimal and iteration use the List API. Alternative fix: if a FIFO semantics is intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList and change the textual instructions to match the Queue type so all artifacts consistently describe the same collection.

issues.description: The Farm collection field representing the animals is inconsistent across artifacts. In the problem statement/UML the attribute is named 'animals' with type List<Animal> and the Part 3 instructions explicitly ask to initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. The template Farm.java contains a TODO placeholder for implementing Farm but no concrete declaration yet. The solution implementation declares the same conceptual field as 'private Queue<Animal> animals' and initializes it with 'new LinkedList<>()', and its getter/setter use Queue<Animal>. Students reading the task (which requires List/ArrayList) could be confused when comparing to the reference solution (which uses Queue/LinkedList) because the collection interface and concrete implementation differ for the same conceptual entity 'Farm.animals', increasing mapping effort and potential misunderstanding about the expected type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm collection type consistent. Update the solution implementation to declare the field as 'private List<Animal> animals', import java.util.ArrayList and java.util.List, initialize it in the no-arg constructor with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', and change the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively (less preferred) update the problem statement/UML to accept Queue/LinkedList, but prefer aligning the solution to the explicit task requirement (List/ArrayList).
